page: Microsoft Azure FX64mds_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The configuration includes 64 virtual CPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features a substantial memory capacity of 1344.0 GB, which translates to 21.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is bundled with 3780 GB of local disk capacity and supports Premium Storage. The processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core capabilities and exceptional memory throughput. The server achieved a top-tier Passmark CPU score of 85402.59 and a top-tier database operations score of 37190.82. Memory bandwidth is highly competitive, with large-block read-only speeds reaching 392.4 GB/sec and write speeds at 170.98 GB/sec, both placing in the top tier. Multi-core stress-ng performance is strong at 70926.61, while single-core performance is average at 2171.29. Static web serving throughput is also top-tier at 97.07 GB/sec. For AI workloads, the system processes 7B model prompts at 292.5 tokens/sec.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated hardware resources, this server represents a high-density memory-optimized tier. The qualitative cost efficiency is driven by the massive RAM allocation and fast local storage, which reduces the need to scale out multiple smaller nodes for large datasets. However, the lack of GPU acceleration limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, though the AMX instructions provide strong CPU-based inference. This configuration is suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale Redis deployments, in-memory analytics, and high-throughput web serving.
